evidence_inputs: The landed change is correct on its own terms: nova/equilibrium/current.py:213-300 partitions cells into full (membership >= 1-1e-14, booked on original vertices via whole_cell) and cut (0 < membership < 1, gathered into batches of 32 and integrated live-ring by live-ring), reproducing the superseded booking to 5.42e-16 relative at 2,098 and 4.45e-16 at 5,158 cells (fresh.log), and clearing its own stated target (sub-250 ms at 5,000) at 85.4 ms.

The node's done_when clause (3) is met in its primary form: identity against the current (inherited vmapped) booking. The alternate form, identity against the closed-form certificate moments, is not delivered -- the six analytic-certificate parametrizations fail in both arms at scripts/prototypes/support/book.py:55, a shared fixture cache-key assertion reached before current.book, and that file is outside the node's write scope. The node records this under follow_ons and sets the fragment plan-verdict partial, which is accurate.

The 10,000-cell rung is unmeasured and recorded pending: the done_when explicitly permits 'record it as pending' when the carrier-requalify device store is unavailable, and the manifest states the diverted 10,000-cell carrier is refused at stencil conditioning. Target achieved to 5,158 cells; the headline 'milliseconds on fine grids' is demonstrated at 5,158, not at 10,000.

Peak device memory falls 7.91 to 0.279 GB (28.4x) at 2,098 cells and 23.13 to 0.728 GB (31.8x) at 5,158 (fresh.log), consistent with the evidence fragment's claim of bounded memory via the 32-cell cut batch.

findings.text: the guard asserts `cells not in lengths` with cells fixed at 17, so it reddens only when a lowered scan's length equals the exact cell count. It fires on the declared regression (negative-control.log shows scan length 17 from reinstating a sequential cell scan), so done_when(5) is guarded, but a sequential cell axis lowered with a different bound -- an outer scan over a padded or fixed-width axis, as the 32-wide cut batch would produce at a different batch width -- would pass. Tightening it to assert no scan axis spans the cell dimension would make the guard independent of the fixture's cell count.

the six analytic-certificate parametrizations -- the §3 closed-form identity gate -- fail in both arms at this shared fixture's cache-key assertion (assert store.group == receipt["machine_cache"]["semantic_key"]) before current.book runs, because the stored device-built machine identity lacks the builder keys and carries a different wall hash (preflight: 2000 e1181cd028835f12 vs 56c89ac4cf893668, 5000 cdccd053cb900cee vs 4c818bdbed936090). The node cannot repair it (file outside its fence) and records it under follow_ons; the effect is that the change's identity against closed-form certificate moments is unverified pending a merged carrier test that supplies matching receipts.
